title: The centre of compatibility in the destiny matrix: the atmosphere inside a couple

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility center: the couple’s atmosphere
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility center: the couple’s shared atmosphere. How it is worked out from two dates, which arcana it holds and how to read them.

short: The centre of a compatibility matrix is the couple’s shared atmosphere: what goes on between two people when nobody is watching. It is worked out from two dates of birth and almost never matches either partner’s own centre. Below: how to find your couple’s centre, which arcana appear there and how often, and how to read the atmosphere in the plus and in the minus.

paragraphs: In a couple’s matrix the centre is the shared atmosphere between the partners. Yuliana Lisovskaya describes it as what lies inside the couple and is not on show: the mood two people live in when they are alone together. In her book it is point A; in the couple reading it is the sphere “The atmosphere inside the couple”.

The centre is read both in the plus and in the minus. The same arcanum gives a couple both a strength and its flip side: passion easily turns into dependence, calm into boredom, honesty into keeping score.

**The centre shows what is between you; the image of the couple shows what others see.** The image is point B, how the union looks to friends and family. Together they answer whether what the couple shows outside matches what goes on inside.

sections.h2: How the couple’s centre is calculated
paragraphs: The couple’s centre is the sum of the two personal centres. If the sum is above 22, its digits are added. The partners’ personal centres stay their own: they describe each of them separately, while the couple’s centre is the space between them.

A restrained Emperor and a quiet Hermit together give Death — an atmosphere of constant renewal that neither of them has alone. **The couple’s centre is not the average of two characters but a third force that appears only in this union.**

sections.h2: Which arcana appear in the couple’s centre
paragraphs: Twenty arcana appear in a couple’s centre — from 3 to 22. A 1 or a 2 never does: a personal centre is never below three, and the sum of two centres does not reduce to 1 or 2. A 3 and a 4 are rare, 0.2% of couples each. Shares are of all pairs of dates of birth from 1900 to 2026; the atmosphere is the caption from our couple reading.

paragraphs: Fifteen, seventeen, nineteen and twenty-one never appear in the centre of a personal matrix, yet they are in the centre of 30% of couples. The Tower, The Devil and The Star are the most common: for almost one couple in three the atmosphere is built around upheavals, a strong pull or a big dream.

sections.h2: How to read the arcanum in the centre
paragraphs: Atmosphere is a background, not an event. The centre does not say what exactly will happen to the couple. It says in what mood the two go through everything else: money, daily life, the union’s tasks.

ul: **In the plus** the arcanum of the centre is what nourishes the couple and what keeps the two holding on to each other. The Devil is a pull you cannot tear yourself away from; Temperance is a calm in which it is easy to agree.
**In the minus** it is the same energy taken to an extreme. The pull turns into dependence and control, the calm into distance where important things go unspoken.
**The shift** from plus to minus usually shows in small things: whatever there is suddenly too much of at home — upheavals, silence, daydreaming — is the signal.

paragraphs: Each arcanum is covered in detail on its own page in [“Arcana in compatibility”](/encyclopedia/compatibility): there is a separate chapter on how it behaves in the couple’s centre.

sections.h2: The centre and the couple’s other points
paragraphs: The centre is not read on its own. For Lisovskaya it is one of five points read together with the couple’s spiritual purpose — its values: the centre, the image of the couple, why the couple met, what fills the union and what can spoil it.

ul: **With the image of the couple** — whether the inside matches the outside. A stormy centre with a calm image means only the two of them know about the storms.
**With what fills the union** — where the couple can draw strength when the atmosphere slides into the minus.
**With what can spoil it** — where the minus of the centre turns into serious quarrels.

sections.h2: Where to see your couple’s centre
paragraphs: Enter two dates of birth into the [compatibility calculator](/compatibility). The couple’s centre and the sphere “The atmosphere inside the couple” are open free: the number, the card and the full text about what is between you. The full reading adds the other spheres, the couple’s karmic tail and the couple’s chakras.

faq.q: What does the centre mean in a compatibility matrix?
faq.a: It is the couple’s shared atmosphere — what is between two people when nobody is watching. In the couple reading the centre is described in the sphere “The atmosphere inside the couple”, and it is read both in the plus and in the minus.

faq.q: How do I work out the couple’s centre?
faq.a: Add the partners’ personal centres; if the sum is above 22, add its digits. The compatibility calculator does it for you: the couple’s centre and the text on its atmosphere are open free.

faq.q: Why can a couple’s centre be 15 when a personal one cannot?
faq.a: A personal centre is calculated from the points of one date, and 15, 17, 19 and 21 never come up there. A couple’s centre is the sum of two centres, and these arcana do appear in it: together in 30% of couples.

faq.q: Which arcanum is best in the couple’s centre?
faq.a: There are no good or bad ones: each arcanum in the centre is read in the plus and in the minus. Calm Temperance can turn into boredom, and a stormy Tower into honesty that holds a couple together for years.

faq.q: How is the couple’s centre different from the image of the couple?
faq.a: The centre is what lies inside the union and is not on show. The image of the couple is how others see the union. They are read together to see whether the outside matches the inside.

faq.q: Can the couple’s centre match one partner’s centre?
faq.a: It can, but only as a coincidence: the couple’s centre is the sum of two centres, not a choice of one of them. Even when the number matches, in a couple it describes the atmosphere between the two, not one person’s character.
